sent_subject: Bruno’s Bowl trial teardown + 90‑day retention test matrix
sent:
Sanjay —

Goal: reduce post‑trial cancels without denting trial CVR. Here’s a focused teardown and a 90‑day retention test plan you can run with ops.

Trial page teardown: what to change this week
- Make post‑trial price and first‑renewal timing unmissable in the hero. Bring “Most plans are £49–£89/month after your trial” up front and add a plain line about when the first renewal happens (right now that lives in the FAQ as “7 days after delivery”). Make it visible before the CTA.
- Replace evergreen “Ends tonight.” If it’s not truly expiring, it erodes trust. Swap for proof (“4.8★ Trustpilot • 12,000+ dogs fed”) or a real limiter only if you actually cap volume.
- Match expectations to the two‑week trial. Test keeping the default first renewal on/just after two weeks versus the current “7 days after delivery,” and let customers pick a different date at checkout.
- Promise the pre‑renewal reminder on the page: “We’ll email you before the first renewal with one‑click options to delay, switch recipes, or pause,” and follow through.
- Keep messaging consistent on pause/cancel timing. The homepage says “pause/cancel 48h before your renewal”; echo that on the trial page near the CTA.
- Post‑checkout confirmation: show the actual renewal date, the expected plan price (use the £49–£89 guidance), a direct “Manage your plan” link, and an “Add to calendar” button. If the account email may take up to 10 minutes, say it there.

90‑day retention test matrix
Primary metric: trial→first‑renewal retention by cohort.
Secondary: pre‑renewal cancel rate, delay rate, support contacts re: timing/portioning, first‑90‑day revenue per acquired customer.

Days 0–30: setup + fast A/Bs
- A/B: Hero clarity (with price + timing) vs control. Measure: trial CVR, pre‑renewal cancels, first‑renewal retention.
- A/B: Urgency treatment. Control = “Ends tonight.” Variant = remove/replace with proof. Measure as above.
- Policy test: Default first renewal on/just after two weeks vs current “7 days after delivery,” with choice at checkout. Measure: first‑renewal retention; “renewed too soon” contacts.
- Reminder test: Add a 48‑hour pre‑renewal email with three buttons: Delay 1 week, Switch recipes, Pause. Control = current flow. Measure: first‑renewal retention; delay→keep vs delay→cancel.
- Onboarding nudge: Day‑3 check‑in asking “Is the portion right?” with 1‑click adjust. Control = none. Measure: adjustments; cancels before renewal.

Days 31–60: step‑downs and expectation shaping
- Plan step‑down at reminder: Offer lower‑frequency or smaller box for price‑sensitive customers. Measure: saves vs ARPU over 60 days.
- Recipe rotation default: Default “chef’s rotation” on vs off. Hypothesis: reduces taste‑fatigue cancels. Measure: taste‑related cancels; retention.
- Social proof placement: Add the Trustpilot strip directly under the CTA on the trial page. Measure: trial CVR and knock‑on retention for that cohort.

Days 61–90: loyalty and save flows (cancellation still one click and simple)
- Cancel‑flow save step: Before confirmation, offer “Pause 2 weeks” or “Step down plan” as a one‑click alternative. Keep the final cancel button clearly available. Measure: saves that remain active 30 days later.
- Second‑box nudge: Small loyalty nudge after a successful first renewal (e.g., thank‑you credit or free add‑on). Measure: retention to third box.

How to project impact (plug your numbers into this)
- Track weekly by cohort: trials started (T), trial CVR, pre‑renewal cancels (C0), first‑renewal retention (R1), second‑renewal retention (R2), average box values (B1 trial, B2, B3), plus CAC if you want payback.
- 90‑day revenue per acquired customer ≈ (B1/T) + R1×(B2/T) + (R1×R2)×(B3/T). Compare variant vs control.
- Decision rule: ship the variant when lift in 90‑day revenue per acquired customer outweighs any CAC change from trial‑page tests.
